Custom business apps · Melbourne

Business software that fits the way your team works.

When every job involves a workaround, another subscription may not fix it. I help Melbourne businesses build custom apps around their own workflows—from a focused internal tool to a tailored job management system.

Start with the work your current software makes awkward

A custom app makes sense when the way your business works consistently falls outside the tools you pay for. That could be a workflow kept in spreadsheets, job information spread across several apps or a team waiting for a vendor to add a feature.

The first version does not have to replace everything. We can build a smaller tool around one workflow, connect it to existing software and learn from real use before expanding it.

I’ve made this change in my own business

We replaced every SaaS app in my business with one in-house app and removed over $80,000 in annual subscriptions. The part I value most is being able to act directly on a team member’s suggestion. Small improvements can go from an idea in the morning to a working change by lunchtime.

That is my own experience, not a forecast for your project. Custom software still has build and running costs, and larger changes need scoping and testing. Read the story behind the $80,000 figure.

What we define before building

  • The core workflow. Which tasks the first release must support, who uses it and what stays in existing software.
  • The records. Where customers, jobs, notes and attachments live, and how they relate.
  • Access and recovery. Permissions, backups, data exports and what happens if the system is unavailable.
  • Ownership and support. Source-code access, documentation, maintenance responsibilities and future changes.
  • The economics. Build costs, hosting, AI usage, maintenance and team time alongside subscriptions you may remove.

A staged build your team can help shape

  1. Walk through real work. Identify the workarounds and agree a useful first scope.
  2. Build a version your team can try. Test the core journey with realistic records and different user roles.
  3. Plan the transition. Check exports, attachments and active jobs before changing the system your team relies on.
  4. Improve from feedback. Use the team’s experience to prioritise what comes next.

Replacing job management software?

Test the exit before choosing a new system. Your current platform’s export options, historical attachments and active jobs can determine the migration effort. A staged cutover with a rollback plan gives you a way to check the new app before relying on it. Start with the job management replacement checklist.

Sometimes an integration is enough. We can compare the options over a coffee in Melbourne or a call and choose the smallest change that solves the real problem.

A few practical questions

Can a custom app replace all my subscriptions?

It may replace some or many, but that depends on what they do and what your business needs. My own result is not a guarantee. The decision should include running costs, maintenance and the effort of migration.

Who owns the app and the data?

Source-code access, data ownership, exports, hosting and support responsibilities should be agreed in the project terms before development. We discuss these as part of scoping.

How long does a custom business app take?

The scope, integrations, data migration and testing determine the timeline. We define a useful first release and agree its delivery plan. The lunchtime example describes small changes in my existing app, not a new app delivered in a few hours.
